AI and automation · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Model drift monitoring

Fabio · Model Monitoring Analyst

A fintech has 14 models in production scoring 600 thousand decisions a week, checked by a scientist when there is time to spare, every 2 or 3 months.

When it runs
Every Monday at 6 a.m., after the weekly scoring batch and the outcomes table update have completed, for the 14 models in the inventory
What it delivers in production
One bulletin per model every Monday at 6:30 a.m. with a traffic light for the stability of inputs, score and performance on matured cohorts; the retraining task, with the diagnosis, opens when the limit persists for two weeks.
Who decides
Diagnoses and opens a task; the committee decides
Effort
Calibrate 26 weeks; 6 weeks bulletin-only
Set up5 steps · 10 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

# Retraining and model monitoring policy

## Colors
PSI below 0.10: GREEN. From 0.10 up to the inventory limit: YELLOW. Above the limit: RED. AUC or KS drop above the limit: RED in performance. Overall traffic light of the model: the worst color among inputs, score and performance.

## Mature cohort
The cohort is the origination month. Mature when the last day of the month plus maturation_days is on or before today. An immature cohort does not count, even with a worse AUC.

## Probable cause
A new band, or one that grew a lot, in an origin variable (channel, product, region): population drift. Same population with a worse outcome: behavioral drift.

## Who decides
The model owner investigates and opens the retraining. Adjusting the approval cutoff belongs to the risk committee.

## Rules with no leeway
- PSI with ln. E.g.: consumer_credit_v7 has origin_channel 1.36, declared_income 0.27 (RED, limit 0.20), age 0.00 (GREEN) and score 0.14 (YELLOW, limit 0.25).
- Approval in points. E.g.: 58.2% against 52.0% = +6.2 points: above 5 and up to 8, retraining task and model risk lead, no committee.
- Mature cohort as of 2026-11-16. E.g.: credit with 90 days: 2026-07 is the most recent mature one (AUC 0.79, drop 0.03 within 0.05); 2026-08 and 2026-09 stay out.
- History counts the current week. E.g.: consumer_credit_v7 RED in inputs in the week of Nov 2 and in the current one: two in a row.
- An isolated YELLOW tags no one. E.g.: card_fraud_v3 with score PSI 0.13 (limit 0.20): record only.
- OTHER MODELS counts all the others by color. E.g.: card_fraud_v3 YELLOW (score) and insurance_propensity_v2 GREEN: 1 green and 1 yellow.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent never retrains, swaps versions or touches the approval cutoff: it opens the task with the diagnosis and the risk committee decides, because changing the cutoff in production without governance is a policy failure that audit and the regulator will point out. The reference changes only when the scientist provides the new training base; recalibrating it with production hides the drift. The tables carry internal identifiers without CPF (individual tax ID) and the bulletin publishes only aggregates. Access to the exports uses a dedicated read credential, with no write permission on the warehouse; the employee's only write is the task in GitHub.

Common mistakes

  • Measuring performance on cohorts that have not matured yet and concluding that the model improved.
  • Looking only at the score PSI and not at each variable's; two variables can offset each other.
  • Updating the reference with recent production to clear the alert, which amounts to switching off the alarm.
  • Confusing population drift (new channel, campaign) with behavioral drift; the actions are different.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Weeks between the start of drift and detectionfrom 7 weeks in the April episode to 1 to 2 weeks, verified in calibration over 26 weeksestimate based on the described routine
Models with a weekly stability checkfrom 14 models reviewed every 2 or 3 months to 14 out of 14 every weekestimate based on the described routine
False red alerts per modelat most 2 in 26 weeks during calibration; monitored monthlyestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Bulletin for week 35, model personal_credit_v7, 41,300 decisions.
INPUT STABILITY (PSI against the training reference): declared_income 0.31 RED (limit 0.20) | origin_channel 0.27 RED | age 0.04 GREEN | relationship_tenure 0.09 GREEN | 44 remaining variables below 0.10
SCORE STABILITY: PSI 0.18 YELLOW; approval rate 58.2% against 52.0% in the reference (+6.2 points)
PERFORMANCE ON MATURED COHORTS (originated 90 days ago): AUC 0.79 against 0.82 in training, a drop of 0.03 within the 0.05 limit; 30-day default 4.9% against 4.1% expected
PROBABLE CAUSE: 38% of the week's decisions came from the 'retail_partner' channel, which does not exist in the training base; declared income in this channel has a 42% lower median. Population drift, not behavioral drift.
HISTORY: second consecutive week in RED on inputs.
ACTION: retraining task opened (#RT-118) for the owner, with a suggestion to include the new channel in the base and review the approval cutoff until the retraining is out. Cutoff adjustment decision: risk committee.
OVERALL MODEL TRAFFIC LIGHT: RED. OTHER 13 MODELS: 11 GREEN, 2 YELLOW (card_fraud_v3 on score PSI 0.12; insurance_propensity_v2 on a KS drop of 0.04).
